items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-04
items.q: Then I played with Rene and he'd come over there. As a matter of fact, I played with Rene here.

ctx.x: Oh, wow. I just wanted to get him straight. Yeah. So I'd know who he was.

Uh-huh. Then I played with Rene and he'd come over there. As a matter of fact, I played with Rene here. But he first known me from over there. Uh, when Jim Robson used to come over there with Sam Morgan, I was a little boy then. And he used to come over there with Sam Morgan when I used to play with him. And then Isaiah Morgan made up him a band. He used to come over there. He used to play with him. I played with Isaiah a long time. And then Tom Albert come to play with my daddy. Well, he told me I was a heard me…
What kind of cornet did he play? Did he play straight or hard?

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-05
items.q: Oh yeah, I played a lot with Renee.

ctx.x: Well, he had a little bit of air on the piano. But play. Ooh, he could play some piano. And never was sober. Never was sober. He stayed right there in the same hotel with us. He wake up in the morning and get drunk. Get drunk when he eat. Twelve o'clock he get drunk. Go to work he's drunk. Come from work he's drunk. But play. Never was late on the job. And never went to sleep. Never went to sleep. But he'd be drunk. Played everything you put in front of him and what you don't put in front of him he played. He was…

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1963-11-21
items.q: I worked with Randy a long time, often and long.

ctx.x: What other bands did you sort of play around with like your son when Tom didn't have a joke? Do you remember any other bands that hired you?

Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. I worked with Randy a long time, often and long. Mm-hmm. I worked with Chris Kelly. I worked with Buddy Petit. I worked with Jack Carey. I worked with Leslie Mayne. I worked with a fella called Big, One-Eyed Big, bass player. Mm-hmm. I worked with him. Oh, I worked with several bands around there, different places they'd go play in there. They'd sit on me there and have nothing but tones. I was in Idol, I stayed busy all the time.

What year did you say that was when you got into New Orleans? I went to New Orleans. I mean, when I got into New Orleans in 1980. Uh-huh. Yeah. But, trying to get some kind of picture of the style of clarinet you were playing then, I think Dick already asked you this. What you're playing now, the clarinet you're playing now, wasn't too much like what you were playing then? No. How was it different then?
